 By Tom Kao October 22, 2026 One of this autumn’s hottest K-dramas, "100 Days of Deception" has put Kim You-jung back in the spotlight. Set during the Japanese occupation of Korea, the historical spy romance sees her starring opposite Got7’s Park Jin-young as Lee Ga-gyeong, a skilled pickpocket who becomes an undercover spy for the independence movement. As secrets and unexpected feelings unfold, her latest role once again showcases her versatility. From psychological thrillers to heart-fluttering romances and historical favourites, here are six of her K-dramas worth revisiting 
 Dear X (2025)
 Kim You-jung takes a darker turn in Dear X , delivering one of her most chilling performances yet. She plays Baek Ah-jin, a top actress who has climbed her way to fame by manipulating those around her, all while hiding her ruthless nature behind a seemingly flawless image. Haunted by a traumatic childhood, she relies on Yoon Jun-seo (Kim Young-dae), who remains devoted to protecting her despite her increasingly destructive actions. But as secrets from her past begin to surface, her carefully constructed world starts to crumble, revealing a strikingly different side of Kim's acting.
 My Demon (2023)
 On a more romantic note, My Demon pairs Kim You-jung with Song Kang in a fantasy love story with a supernatural twist. Kim plays Do Do-hee, a fiercely independent heiress whose life becomes entangled with Jeong Gu-won, a 200-year-old demon whose powers mysteriously transfer to her after he saves her life. With Do-hee caught in a dangerous family inheritance battle and Gu-won desperate to regain his powers, the two enter a contract marriage that slowly turns into something more. Between their playful chemistry and darker family secrets, there are plenty of heart-fluttering moments.

 Backstreet Rookie (2020)
 Showing off her more playful side, Kim You-jung stars opposite Ji Chang-wook in the romantic comedy Backstreet Rookie . She plays Jung Saet-byul, a spirited young woman who reunites with her longtime crush, Choi Dae-hyun, after landing a part-time job at his struggling convenience store. Although Dae-hyun initially doubts her because of her troublesome past, Saet-byul soon proves herself a capable employee. Things get complicated, however, when their growing closeness begins to affect his relationship with his girlfriend. Packed with amusing misunderstandings and everyday chaos, the drama brings out Kim's lively charm.
 Lovers of the Red Sky (2021)
 For those who enjoy historical romances with a touch of fantasy, Lovers of the Red Sky is worth revisiting. Kim You-jung plays Hong Cheon-ki, a gifted painter who was born blind but mysteriously regains her sight. Set in a fictional dynasty inspired by the Joseon era, the story follows her reunion with Ha Ram (Ahn Hyo-seop), a blind astrologer she first met as a child. As their feelings grow, the pair become caught in royal power struggles and a dangerous supernatural curse, making their love story anything but straightforward.
 Clean with Passion for Now (2018)
 Opposites attract in Clean with Passion for Now , a romantic comedy that sees Kim You-jung playing Gil Oh-sol, a cheerful but messy young woman juggling part-time jobs to support her family. Things take an unexpected turn when she lands a job at a cleaning company run by Jang Seon-gyeol (Yoon Kyun-sang), a wealthy CEO with an intense fear of germs. Their completely different lifestyles lead to plenty of awkward and amusing encounters, but the two gradually grow closer as Oh-sol helps him face his fears. It's a charming watch that brings out Kim's down-to-earth side.
 Love in the Moonlight (2016)
 Of course, no Kim You-jung drama roundup would feel complete without Love in the Moonlight . One of her most beloved works, the historical romance follows Hong Ra-on, a young woman who disguises herself as a man and earns a living writing love letters for others. After a chance encounter with Crown Prince Lee Yeong (Park Bo-gum), she unexpectedly ends up serving as a palace eunuch, where their growing feelings become complicated by her hidden identity and royal power struggles. Filled with tender moments and palace intrigue, the drama helped establish Kim as a leading actress.
